name: SIA Project 25 26
description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section). If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:
- Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved. Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
- Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description. Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

highLevelGoals: Allow registered citizens to submit detailed reports about urban inconveniences, including location, description, category, and photos, to facilitate the identification of problems in the city.
Require citizens to register and confirm their email address to ensure the authenticity of report submitters and maintain the integrity of the participation system.
Notify citizens of changes in the status of their submitted reports through the platform and email to maintain transparency and trust in the public administration.
Enable citizens to exchange messages with municipal operators regarding their reports to clarify issues and provide additional information.
Allow citizens to follow reports submitted by other citizens and receive notifications about their progress to foster community engagement and awareness.
Allow citizens to control the visibility of their identity in public reports and manage notification settings to respect their privacy choices.
Enable unregistered visitors to view the interactive map, summary tables, and public statistics of urban issues to promote transparency without requiring an account.
Allow municipality staff to perform preliminary reviews of submitted reports to determine their validity and decide whether to accept or reject them with mandatory explanations for rejections.
Enable staff to assign accepted reports to the appropriate technical offices or external companies based on the problem category to ensure efficient resource allocation.
Allow staff to update the lifecycle status of reports (e.g., In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved) to accurately reflect the state of urban maintenance activities.
Enable staff to communicate with external maintenance personnel and update report statuses when external companies resolve issues outside the system.
Allow external maintenance personnel with system access to update the status of assigned reports and mark them as resolved upon completion of work.
Enable external maintenance personnel to exchange comments and information with municipality staff regarding specific reports to facilitate problem resolution.
Allow administrators to configure automatic assignment rules for specific report categories to external companies to streamline the workflow and reduce manual intervention.
Provide administrators with access to private statistics, charts, and tables to analyze report trends, identify recurring issues, and optimize municipal resource planning.
Enable administrators to manage user registrations, roles, and access permissions to ensure the security and proper functioning of the participation platform.
lowLevelGoals: The system creates a new report record with the provided title, description, category, and location coordinates, and returns the unique report ID.
The system accepts a binary file upload, associates it with the specified report ID, and returns a URL or reference to the stored image.
The system creates a new user account with the provided email and password, generates a unique verification token, and stores the user in an unverified state.
The system validates the provided email verification token, updates the user's status to verified, and enables full account functionality.
The system retrieves the current status and history of status changes for the specified report ID and returns the data to the authenticated user.
The system sends an email notification to the citizen's registered address containing the new status and a link to the report details.
The system creates a new message record associated with the specified report ID, authored by the citizen, and stores it in the report's communication thread.
The system retrieves the list of messages exchanged between the citizen and municipality staff for the specified report ID.
The system adds the authenticated citizen to the list of followers for the specified report ID.
The system removes the authenticated citizen from the list of followers for the specified report ID.
The system updates the user's profile settings to specify whether their name and avatar are visible on public reports.
The system updates the user's notification preferences to enable or disable specific types of alerts (e.g., status changes, new messages).
The system retrieves the list of public reports with their location, category, and status for display on the interactive map without requiring authentication.
The system retrieves aggregated public statistics (e.g., total reports, resolved count, average resolution time) for display to unregistered visitors.
The system updates the status of the specified report to 'Accepted' and records the staff member's approval action.
The system updates the status of the specified report to 'Rejected', requires a mandatory reason string, and records the staff member's rejection action.
The system associates the specified report ID with a designated technical office or external company ID, updating the report's assignment field.
The system updates the lifecycle status of the specified report to 'In Progress' and logs the timestamp and staff member responsible.
The system updates the lifecycle status of the specified report to 'Resolved' and logs the completion timestamp.
The system creates a message record from the staff member to the external maintenance personnel associated with the report, facilitating off-system coordination.
The system updates the status of the specified report to 'Resolved' based on input from external maintenance personnel, bypassing internal staff confirmation if configured.
The system creates a message record from the external maintenance personnel to the municipality staff regarding the specified report.
The system creates or updates a rule that automatically assigns reports of a specific category to a designated external company or office.
The system retrieves private statistical data, including detailed breakdowns by category, office, and time period, for administrative analysis.
The system updates the role or access permissions of an existing user account based on administrative input.

baselineCritiques.actors: The actors defined are mostly appropriate for the system's description. However, there is a redundancy between "Municipality Staff" and "External Maintenance Personnel," as both seem to handle report management, which could lead to confusion. Additionally, the role of "Administrator" overlaps with "System manager," which might be better consolidated into one clear actor. The "Guest" role is correctly identified but could be more explicitly named (e.g., "Unregistered User") for clarity.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the software description. All goals are functional and address the core functionalities of Participium, including citizen reporting, staff management, external maintenance coordination, and administrative tasks. No contradictions or omissions were found.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are well-aligned with the high-level goals and actors, covering all necessary functional aspects of the Participium system. There are no contradictions or omissions in the provided low-level goals. All goals are specific, actionable, and directly correspond to actions performed by the actors as described.
